newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Mauritius not seen meeting all sugar export quotas.
newsitem.headline: Mauritius not seen meeting all sugar export quotas.

text.p: Mauritius will not fulfil its Special Preferential Sugar (SPS) export quota to European (cane) sugar refiners because of lower-than-expected production in 1996, the Public Relations Office of the Sugar Industry (Prosi) said in on Tuesday.
The Mauritius Chamber of Agriculture has revised 1996 production forecasts to 590,000 tonnes from an initial estimate of 610,000 tonnes, citing adverse climatic conditions.

"For 1996/97, the share of Mauritius from the tonnage allocated to ACP (African, Caribbean and Pacific) states according to the SPS Agreement is 75,000 tonnes. It is now expected that Mauritius will deliver around 45,000 tonnes of these 75,000 tonnes," Prosi said in a statement.
Prosi added that Mauritius would completely meet all its other 1996/97 export commitments of 507,000 tonnes under the Lome Sugar Protocol and 24,000 tonnes to the United States.
Prosi said the Mauritian export shortfall of 30,000 tonnes would be met by one or more of the other 15 ACP states which signed the SPS agreement with the European Union in mid 1995.
The SPS was a collective engagement and if there was a shortfall by one country, for example because of climatic conditions, this would be met by the other countries.
A sugar industry official told Reuters: "Future quotas to Mauritius will not be affected because of the collective engagement."
The industry official said revenues from sugar exports for 1996/97 had been revised down by some 100 million rupees to 8.2 billion rupees.
In 1995/96, Mauritius met its export commitments under the Sugar Protocol and a quota of 23,000 tonnes to the U.S.
But it failed to meet an allocation of some 90,000 tonnes under the SPS Agreement with only 13,000 tonnes supplied.
Total sugar export revenues last year were posted at 6.9 billion rupees.
In 1995, Mauritian sugar production was posted at 539,521 tonnes. At the time, produce was adversely affected by cyclonic weather at the start of the year.
